data.body_html:
Choosing between the Azimut 39 and the Fairline Targa 12m for your Marbella boat rental in 2045? Both depart from Puerto Banús, but they cater to different priorities. The Azimut 39 offers a flybridge for social lounging and carries 11 passengers at a fixed all-inclusive price. The Fairline Targa 12m is a sportier, open-deck cruiser for up to 10 guests, with bespoke pricing. This comparison breaks down specs, capacity, and value to help you decide.

Size and Passenger Capacity

The Azimut 39 measures 12.5 metres and can take 11 passengers. The Fairline Targa 12m is 12 metres long with a capacity of 10 passengers. If you have a group of 11, the Azimut is your only choice. For 10 or fewer, both work, but the Azimut’s extra half-metre provides a slightly larger cockpit and flybridge area.

Price and Inclusions

The Azimut 39 is priced at €749 for 2 hours up to €2,299 for 8 hours, with everything included: skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT. The Fairline Targa 12m has pricing on request via WhatsApp. Both charters include the same comprehensive package—no hidden extras. For budget certainty, the Azimut 39 wins.

Design and Onboard Experience

The Azimut 39 features a flybridge—perfect for sunbathing and panoramic views of La Concha and the Golden Mile. The Fairline Targa 12m has a sleek, open-plan layout with a large aft cockpit, ideal for waterside dining and quick access to the swim platform. Choose the Azimut for elevated lounging, the Fairline for a sportier, more intimate vibe.

Performance and Speed

The Fairline Targa 12m is faster, reaching 30–35 knots, compared to the Azimut 39’s 28–30 knots. If you want to zip from Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro or Estepona quickly, the Fairline delivers. For a relaxed cruise past Cabopino or Sotogrande, the Azimut’s pace is ample—and fuel is included either way.

Itinerary Flexibility

Both boats depart from Puerto Banús and can visit Marbella Marina, Cabopino, Cala Cortés, or Estepona. The Azimut’s flybridge is better for longer days (8-hour charter) as guests can move between sun and shade. The Fairline’s open deck suits shorter, active trips—think swimming stops and water toys. For a full-day exploration, the Azimut offers more comfort.

Which Boat Should You Choose?

Pick the Azimut 39 if you want a fixed price, a flybridge, and capacity for 11 guests. It’s ideal for social groups and sunset cruises. Pick the Fairline Targa 12m if you prioritise speed, a sporty design, and don’t mind requesting a custom quote. Both deliver a premium Marbella charter experience.
